# Tailwind Layout Builder Skill

**Category:** Tech Skills > Frontend > Tailwind CSS

## Purpose

Provides specialized knowledge, step-by-step procedures, and quality standards for Tailwind Layout Builder operations using Tailwind CSS technology. This skill encapsulates technology-specific best practices, design patterns, performance optimization techniques, and production-grade implementation guidance for Tailwind CSS within Frontend development.

## When to Use

- When building responsive page layouts with Tailwind CSS
- When implementing complex grid and flexbox layouts
- When designing mobile-first responsive components
- When Tailwind CSS-specific technical expertise is required
- When best practices for Tailwind CSS technology stack must be applied
- When production-grade Tailwind CSS implementation guidance is needed

## Capabilities

- Build responsive layouts with Tailwind breakpoints
- Implement CSS Grid layouts with Tailwind utilities
- Create flexbox-based component layouts
- Use container queries for component-level responsiveness
- Design mobile-first responsive patterns

## Procedure

1. Analyze layout requirements and breakpoints
2. Design mobile-first layout strategy
3. Implement layout with Tailwind grid and flex utilities
4. Add responsive modifiers for breakpoints
5. Test responsive behavior across viewports
6. Optimize utility usage for minimal CSS output

## Anti-Hallucination Rules

- Do not use Tailwind classes not available in the installed version
- Verify container query support in the target Tailwind version
- Do not fabricate version numbers, API endpoints, or library names
- Always cite the specific documentation, RFC, or standard being referenced
- If technology-specific data is unavailable, explicitly state the gap and request clarification
- Never assume features exist in a specific version without verification

## Quality Checks

- Layout is responsive across all target viewports
- Utility classes follow Tailwind conventions
- CSS output is optimized with purging
- All code examples must be syntactically valid and tested
- Cross-reference findings against official documentation
- Flag any assumptions made during analysis with explicit markers
- Validate all performance claims with reproducible benchmarks
- Ensure all recommendations follow Tailwind CSS community best practices
